claims.statement: The root pom.xml pins org.codehaus.mojo:flatten-maven-plugin to 1.9.0 with flattenMode=resolveCiFriendliesOnly (executing at clean and process-resources phases, updatePomFile=true, expanding dependencyManagement and dependencies) to resolve the CI-friendly ${revision} placeholders (currently <revision>2.2.0-SNAPSHOT</revision>); the pin comment records that 1.8.0's CI-friendly interpolator threw an NPE (mojohaus/flatten-maven-plugin#523), fixed in 1.9.0, and deployed POMs therefore carry fully resolved versions.

ARDoCo requires JDK 21 and Maven 3.9+; each module tree ships its own .mvn/maven.config (parallel -T1C builds) and .mvn/jvm.config (dynamic agent loading, tiered-compilation limits, jdk.compiler add-exports) so plain Maven invocations inside core/, tlr/, or inconsistency-detection/ pick up the tuned JVM and parallelism settings.

The reactor consists of three trees aggregated by io.github.ardoco:parent: core (framework/common + framework/text-provider-json, pipeline-core, tests-base), tlr (pipeline-tlr, stages-tlr with artemis, code-traceability, connection-generator, model-provider, recommendation-generator, text-extraction, text-preprocessing, and tests-tlr under the default complete profile), and inconsistency-detection (pipeline-id, stages-id with artemis-inconsistency-detection, inconsistency-detection, and programming-language-inconsistency-detection, plus stages-id/architectural-style-pattern-inconsistency-detection aggregated directly by parent-id, and tests-inconsistency); the deployment profiles drop the test modules, skip test compilation, and GPG-sign with the pinned KIT key.

The root POM pins shared versions as properties (SLF4J 2.0.20, JUnit Jupiter 6.1.3, Eclipse Collections 13.0.0, JavaParser 3.28.2, Mockito 5.24.0, Stanford CoreNLP 4.6.0, ANTLR 4.13.2, Jackson 3 3.3.0, Jackson 2 2.23.0, metrics 0.3.0) and in dependencyManagement (the Jackson 2 and Jackson 3 BOM imports — the com.fasterxml.jackson:jackson-bom 2.23.0 import only aligns transitive Jackson 2 users such as langchain4j — archunit-junit5 1.5.1, commons-io 2.22.0, commons-lang3 3.22.0, commons-text 1.15.0, httpclient5 5.6.5, assertj-core 3.27.7, Eclipse Collections, Eclipse JGit 7.8.0.202609011348-r, JUnit Jupiter, Mockito, reflections 0.10.2, SLF4J); opennlp-tools 2.5.11 is pinned separately in core/framework/common/pom.xml (PorterStemmer used by ArCoTL NameComparisonUtils, which also lemmatizes via a local Stanford CoreNLP tokenize,pos,lemma pipeline), tlr/stages-tlr/model-provider imports dev.langchain4j:langchain4j-bom 1.19.0 and pins io.github.ardoco:magika 0.7.0, and core/framework/text-provider-json pins com.networknt:json-schema-validator 3.0.9.

Spotless (3.10.4) is configured once in the root pluginManagement and inherited by every module: Eclipse formatter profile from {module}/formatter.xml, import order from {module}/spotless.importorder (java, javax, org, com, then rest), the MIT license header file, unused-import removal, sortPom for POMs, trailing-whitespace/newline normalization for Markdown and .gitignore, and ratchetFrom origin/main so only files changed relative to origin/main are reformatted.

JSpecify nullness is enforced by generating @NullMarked package-info.java files via org.fuchss:jspecify-maven-plugin 0.1.0 in the process-sources phase into each module's source directory; the generated files are git-ignored and org.jspecify:jspecify:1.0.1 is a root-POM dependency, so all modules are null-marked by default without per-module setup.

The core/tests-base module hosts the ArchUnit suites inherited by the test trees: ArchitectureTest enforces the layered pipeline architecture — now including an Artemis layer alongside the stage layers — and stage-boundary naming rules; BasicArchitectureTest restricts @Configurable fields to AbstractConfigurable subclasses, forces TraceLink subclasses to be final, confines Jackson ObjectMapper creation/configuration to JsonHandling, bans Jackson 2 (com.fasterxml.jackson.core/databind) in favor of Jackson 3 (tools.jackson), restricts System.getenv access to the Environment utility (noGetEnv), bans forEach side effects, and requires Eclipse Collections over JDK collection types in interfaces; DeterministicArdocoTest forbids unordered JDK collections outside @Deterministic-annotated classes (excluding ..tests.., ..metrics.., ..magika..) and pushes HashMap/HashSet usage toward the linked variants.

The build's current version baseline is the CI-friendly <revision>2.2.0-SNAPSHOT</revision> property in the root POM (resolved by the pinned flatten-maven-plugin, spotless.version=3.10.4), and the root POM's global dependency block applies jspecify 1.0.1 plus the test-scoped archunit-junit5, assertj-core, and junit-jupiter stack to every module; docs/** and openwiki/** paths are excluded from CI Maven verify.

The root format.yml workflow runs on pull requests to main and on workflow_dispatch: it checks out with submodules and full history via actions/checkout@v7, determines the Java major version inline by probing maven.compiler.target, maven.compiler.release, and java.version in the POM with `mvn help:evaluate` (the job errors out if none resolves), sets up Temurin with Maven caching via actions/setup-java@v6, runs `mvn -B spotless:apply`, and auto-commits the reformatted files with the message 'Apply formatting changes' via stefanzweifel/git-auto-commit-action@v7 — so Spotless violations on a PR are fixed by a bot commit rather than failing the build.

The docs.yml workflow (push to main or v** tags touching docs/**, openwiki/**, or the workflow) destructively republishes the GitHub Wiki: it wipes the wiki except .git, copies /docs to the wiki root plus the openwiki folder to wiki/openwiki, and renders each root-level /openwiki/*.md as OpenWiki-<name>.md in the wiki root namespace with same-directory links rewritten to OpenWiki-<name> — therefore OpenWiki pages must stay flat in /openwiki/*.md and quickstart must not be deleted (OpenWiki-quickstart is linked as the entry point from docs/Home.md and the sidebar).

The openwiki.yml workflow runs weekly (cron 0 6 * * 1, Monday 06:00 UTC) and via workflow_dispatch, delegates to the shared ardoco/actions openwiki reusable workflow passing the OPENROUTER_API_KEY secret, and declares contents: write and pull-requests: write at the call site; the reusable workflow performs the commit-relevance check, installs OpenWiki, runs openwiki --update, and opens the update PR.

Snapshots are published to the Sonatype Central Snapshots repository (https://central.sonatype.com/repository/maven-snapshots/, distributionManagement plus a snapshot resolution repository) and releases by central-publishing-maven-plugin 0.11.0 with autoPublish=true, waitUntil=published, and per-tree deployment names ardoco, ardoco-core, ardoco-tlr, and ardoco-id; release builds use the deployment profiles that GPG-sign with the pinned KIT key and skip test compilation.

All environment lookups go through the Environment utility backed by dotenv-java: if a .env file exists in the working directory it is loaded once at class initialization, and Environment.getEnv(key) returns the .env value first, falling back to system environment variables (so .env overrides system env) and returning null for missing variables; getEnvNonNull logs an error for missing variables but still returns null, and the ArchUnit noGetEnv rule forbids every other class from calling System.getenv, making Environment the single environment-variable gateway.

The StanfordCoreNLP microservice is selected per text, not at startup: TextProcessor uses the remote service only when NLP_PROVIDER_SOURCE=microservice and an authenticated health request to <MICROSERVICE_URL>/stanfordnlp/health answers 'Microservice is healthy'; it retries remote processing on IOException or JacksonException up to two attempts, then falls back to embedded local CoreNLP, and degrades to local processing immediately on InvalidJsonException/NotConvertableException — with defaults from config.properties (nlpProviderSource=microservice, microserviceUrl=http://localhost:8080) overridden by the NLP_PROVIDER_SOURCE and MICROSERVICE_URL environment variables.

LLM integration in tlr/stages-tlr/model-provider is configured via environment variables and made reproducible: LargeLanguageModel pins built-in OpenAI models to dated snapshots (gpt-4o-2024-08-06, gpt-4.1-2025-04-14, gpt-5-2025-08-07, plus the 2026-dated GPT-5.x family such as gpt-5.5-2026-04-23 and gpt-5.4-nano-2026-03-17) with temperature 0.0 (temperature 1.0 only for the GPT_5 and GPT_5_5 variants) and requires OPENAI_ORGANIZATION_ID and OPENAI_API_KEY; Ollama models target OLLAMA_HOST with basic-auth headers from OLLAMA_USER/OLLAMA_PASSWORD or an OpenAI-compatible client when OLLAMA_TOKEN is set, and OPENAI_MODEL_NAME/OLLAMA_MODEL_NAME expose generic variants; all models apply SEED (default 422413373, invalid values abort), and create() wraps each model in CachedChatLanguageModel, which persists a per-model prompt-response map to <name>-cache.json under LLM_CACHE_DIR (default .cache-llm/) serving repeated line-ending-normalized prompts without provider calls and logging cache I/O failures instead of failing the run; the ArTEMiS connection stage (tlr/stages-tlr/artemis) additionally requires OPENAI_API_KEY for the fixed text-embedding-3-large embedding model.

sample.env documents the operational environment variables in three areas: NLP preprocessing (NLP_PROVIDER_SOURCE, MICROSERVICE_URL, SCNLP_SERVICE_USER, SCNLP_SERVICE_PASSWORD), LLM integration (OPENAI_API_KEY, OPENAI_ORGANIZATION_ID, OPENAI_MODEL_NAME, OLLAMA_HOST, OLLAMA_USER, OLLAMA_PASSWORD, OLLAMA_TOKEN, OLLAMA_MODEL_NAME, MODEL_NAME_NER, LLM_CACHE_DIR), and reproducibility (SEED); MODEL_NAME_NER is only a template placeholder with no consumer in this codebase, as the NER connection stage uses the fixed OpenAI embedding model text-embedding-3-large.

ARDoCo depends on external repositories for services and evaluation: the StanfordCoreNLP-Provider-Service microservice (REST wrapper for CoreNLP with credential-based basic authentication), the LiSSA framework for generic LLM+IR-based TLR, the benchmark repository (datasets and gold standards, also bundled as test resources under core/tests-base), the evaluator (io.github.ardoco:metrics), traceview-v2 for visualizing TLR/ID outputs, and ardoco/actions for the reusable CI workflows.

The integration tests in tests-tlr and tests-inconsistency run under Maven Failsafe: the LLM-based ones are @Disabled('Only for manual execution') (e.g. ArtemisIT, ArtemisInExArchIT, ArtemisInTransarcIT, ExArchIT, and the ID ArTEMiS/architectural-style-pattern/programming-language evaluation ITs), and the TLR ArTEMiS/ExArch ITs additionally assume via Assumptions that OPENAI_API_KEY or OLLAMA_HOST is set and that the CI environment variable is absent (in @BeforeAll or per test method), offering mutipleRuns-gated multi-run variants (@DisabledIfEnvironmentVariable on the single-run, @EnabledIfEnvironmentVariable on the multi-run methods); the non-LLM InconsistencyDetectionEvaluationIT carries no @Disabled and therefore executes under Failsafe on every mvn verify, with only its baseline method gated by the testBaseline environment variable; the test trees are refreshed from ardoco/IntegrationTests via the update_integration_tests.sh git-subtree sync (git subtree pull --prefix tests/integration-tests) present in the tlr and inconsistency-detection trees.

The root verify.yml workflow runs Maven verify on push to main and on pull requests (paths-ignore docs/** and openwiki/**, tags v* ignored) by delegating to the reusable ardoco/actions maven.yml with deploy=false — the root call site does not set with-submodules, unlike the module-tree verify.yml copies — and passes empty CENTRAL_USER, CENTRAL_TOKEN, and GPG_KEY secrets so CI verifies without publishing.

The three module-tree Format workflows (core/.github/workflows/format.yml, tlr/.github/workflows/format.yml, inconsistency-detection/.github/workflows/format.yml) are identical copies that replicate the root Format workflow step for step (same pull_request-to-main and workflow_dispatch triggers, inline POM-based Java-version probe, `mvn -B spotless:apply`, git-auto-commit-action@v7 'Apply formatting changes' commit) but lag the root on action versions: they still pin actions/checkout@v6 and actions/setup-java@v5 where the root uses actions/checkout@v7 and actions/setup-java@v6.

The repository root AGENTS.md carries an OPENWIKI:START/OPENWIKI:END block defining the OpenWiki maintenance contract, and CLAUDE.md delegates to it via an @AGENTS.md reference so the same contract governs Claude sessions.

The AGENTS.md OpenWiki contract treats openwiki/ as optional just-in-time context, not required startup reading: agents must not enumerate, preload, or search wikis at task start, and should use retrieval only when the user asks for it, when unfamiliar architecture or dependency behavior materially affects the task, or when source inspection leaves an important uncertainty — stopping once the question is grounded.

The contract prescribes the retrieval tooling: openwiki_search for just-in-time context and openwiki_read for complete sections; if search returns workspace_required, ask which listed workspace to use and retry with its ID; openwiki_list_workspaces/openwiki_list_wikis discover workspace membership; when retrieval tools are unavailable, fall back to reading openwiki/quickstart.md and following its links.

The contract makes source code and tests authoritative — a brief's unknowns and review items are verification gaps, not automatic requirements — and prefers the narrowest quiet validation that proves the changed behavior while preserving complete failure output.

The contract forbids hand-editing generated OpenWiki pages unless explicitly asked; the documented maintenance process refreshes generated pages after source changes, and agents must check the process's configuration and completed runs (weekly openwiki.yml schedule, Monday 06:00 UTC plus workflow_dispatch, delegating to the ardoco/actions reusable workflow with the OPENROUTER_API_KEY secret) before relying on automatic updates.

Snapshot deployment to the GitLab package registry: the deploy-snapshot.yml workflow triggers only via workflow_dispatch and delegates to the reusable ardoco/actions maven-snapshot.yml with gitlab-project-id 203206 (the Maven package registry of the read-only mirror project on gitlab.kit.edu) and secrets: inherit; it only deploys -SNAPSHOT versions and requires the GITLAB_SNAPSHOT_TOKEN secret, a GitLab group deploy token with the write_package_registry scope. All four tree POMs also declare the read-only ardocoSnapshots resolution repository (https://gitlab.kit.edu/api/v4/groups/253644/-/packages/maven), and a manual path exists via `mvn -Pdeployment -DskipTests -Dgpg.skip package deploy:deploy` with an altDeploymentRepository pointing at the project registry, authenticated by a Private-Token (personal/group access token) or Deploy-Token (deploy token) header configured in ~/.m2/settings.xml.

The root POM pluginManagement pins maven-surefire-plugin 3.6.1 and maven-failsafe-plugin 3.6.1, and the failsafe execution binds the integration-test and verify goals to the integration-test phase, so `mvn clean verify` runs both the Surefire unit/architecture tests and the Failsafe integration tests.

Maven dependency updates are managed by Renovate, not Dependabot: the root renovate.json only extends local>ArDoCo/actions:renovate-preset (inheriting the shared preset from the ardoco/actions repository), and there is no root .github/dependabot.yml — only the three module trees carry inert dependabot.yml files for their standalone-repository use.

The inconsistency-detection tree declares the JaCoCo Maven plugin in its build plugins without a version pin or any executions, so it does not instrument anything by default; the pipeline-id module defines an extra default-active test-dependencies profile that pulls the pipeline-core test-jar, while pipeline-tlr wires the same test-jar directly in its dependencies.

LargeLanguageModel sets a 10-minute timeout on OpenAI chat models and 15 minutes on Ollama chat models, while the OpenAI-compatible client path used when OLLAMA_TOKEN is set (with OLLAMA_HOST reused as the base URL) uses a 30-minute timeout; all three paths apply temperature 0.0 and the SEED.
